sources.title: How a Pareto answer gets made
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27 access: the mechanism selects frontier and open models for each request and blends their outputs into one answer; it explicitly distinguishes this from handing a prompt to one model and says composition can change. No learned total, active-parameter convention, fixed member list or named base checkpoint is disclosed.

sources.title: Unbiased terms defining Pareto and its license
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27 access: the definition of Pareto describes synthesized outputs from multiple underlying LLMs accessed through company arrangements. Section 2(c) permits changing the underlying composition. The terms name no constituent checkpoint and publish no learned total or activated-parameter count.

sources.title: About Unbiased
sources.evidence: Identifies Circuit & Chisel as the company building Unbiased and Pareto as its first model. Supports retaining the Unbiased product/developer brand.

sources.title: Original Union Alpha release and confirmed Pareto identity
sources.evidence: The original distributor explicitly dates public release September 16,2026, states that Union Alpha was developed/operated by Unbiased and revealed as Pareto, and records text/image input, text output and 262144 context. The free stealth period is over. This establishes public preview availability before the September 17 named listing.

sources.title: Pareto 26.10 release hub identifying the earlier 26.9 version
sources.evidence: Explicitly identifies Union Alpha as later revealed to be Pareto 26.9. Separately states that the current pareto default selects 26.10 and that pareto-26.9 remains available. The new 1M context belongs to 26.10, not the original September record.

sources.title: Exact Pareto 26.9 endpoint metadata
sources.evidence: Unbiased endpoint unbiased/pareto-26.9-20260917 documents 262144 context and 131072 max completion, text/image input and text output, tools and tool_choice with auto supported. Current provider slug creation is October 13; it is not the first public release date.

sources.title: Current resolution of the original unversioned provider id
sources.evidence: The frozen unversioned path now returns id ~unbiased/pareto-latest, name Pareto Latest, description that it redirects to the latest Pareto family model, and no endpoints. The original September 26.9 release must not be reinterpreted as a newly released 26.10 checkpoint.

sources.title: Unbiased product changes and model alias history
sources.evidence: October 1 entry distinguishes opt-in 26.10-preview from the then-default pareto. October 15 entry moves pareto to 26.10 and preserves 26.9. September entries show earlier platform/API operation but do not identify an earlier public release day for the exact 26.9 revision.

sources.title: Public Pareto API specification
sources.evidence: Documents OpenAI/Anthropic-format requests, tool definitions and assistant tool_calls with text responses. No dedicated public reasoning control is declared in the core specification. This absence does not prove the composite lacks reasoning ability.

sources.title: Current Pareto 26.10 model card, checked for older model disclosures
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27 access: the later 26.10 model card explicitly compares Pareto 26.9, including its September 20 DeepSWE result. Comparison columns and plots report score and USD per task, not total or active parameters. The card gives no fixed constituent list, named unchanged backbone or size convention for 26.9; competitor benchmark labels do not identify blend members.

sources.title: Developer evaluation harness cascade result types
sources.evidence: Reopened pinned original source October 27. CascadeRunResult and TaskScore contain optional gateway/cascade telemetry, stage, escalation, classifier tier, agreement method and finalModel fields. These are generic benchmark interfaces, with no 26.9 deployment composition or learned/active counts; the harness license does not license Pareto weights.

sources.title: October 1 launch notes describing the prior Pareto 26.9 stealth trial
sources.evidence: The developer says it put Pareto 26.9 on OpenRouter, OpenCode and Cloudflare AI Gateway under a made-up name two weeks earlier. Corroborates the original 26.9 identity and earlier public trial, separate from the October 26.10 preview.

sources.title: Union Alpha operator reveal post
sources.evidence: Direct access returned403. Not used as independently accessed evidence; the accessible original distributor and developer release pages establish identity and public-preview date.

sources.title: Current Pareto developer documentation, fresh parameter and lineage review
sources.evidence: Accessed October 27. The developer repeats that Pareto selects frontier and open models per request and blends outputs. Endpoint, SDK, token-limit and model-string instructions do not name a constituent checkpoint, unchanged base-model lineage, total size or activated-parameter accounting convention.

sources.title: Pareto 26.10 stable release notes, checked for original 26.9 lineage and size
sources.evidence: October 15 original release post, reopened October 27, says several frontier and open models work on every request. It explicitly keeps pareto-26.9 live while the unversioned alias moves to 26.10. It publishes prices and the later context size, but no component identities or total/active parameter count for either release; no unchanged checkpoint lineage is asserted.

name.note: Add the original release version to distinguish the frozen September model from the mutable latest alias and October 26.10 releases.

developer.note: Retain the developer/product brand; its legal operator is Circuit & Chisel.

family.note: The developer versions the Pareto family as 26.9 and 26.10.

release_date.note: Earliest explicit public availability is the September 16 Union Alpha stealth preview, whose identity is confirmed by the distributor and developer. September 17 is the named Pareto listing/reveal; October 13 is the later versioned-provider slug. Earlier generic platform changes do not establish a release date for this exact revision.

open_weights.note: Proprietary hosted composite with service-use rights; no single released Pareto weight artifact. Public constituent models or the MIT evaluation harness do not make Pareto itself open-weight.

license.note: Descriptive classification explicitly supported by the developer service terms. Do not copy licenses of undisclosed constituent models or the public evaluation code.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 review of original mechanism, terms, later model-card comparisons, developer docs and release notes finds no nominal total or named unchanged base checkpoint for Pareto 26.9. The provider describes blended outputs from selected frontier/open models, not a disclosed single model. Do not sum hypothetical constituents or transfer competitor sizes.

active_parameters_b.note: Separately rechecked October 27. The later original comparison card labels Pareto 26.9 but reports scores and task costs, with no activated-parameter column or convention. No per-request learned-weight count or named unchanged constituent lineage is established; changing multi-model composition does not support assigning one member's active count.

architecture.note: System-level design is a multi-model blend, not a disclosed single dense, MoE or hybrid neural checkpoint. Underlying network identities and architectures are undisclosed; combining model outputs is not evidence of neural mixture-of-experts routing. Generic cascade harness types do not identify the exact production 26.9 stack.

context_window.note: Exact documented hosted 26.9 limit. Retain 262144; the later 26.10 one-million-token window belongs to a different release. This is an endpoint contract, not an inferred shared constituent positional limit.

modalities.note: Original stealth and exact 26.9 endpoint both document native text/image requests and text responses. Server tools or later product integrations do not add output modalities.

reasoning.note: Neither absent reasoning controls nor benchmark scores establish a binary reasoning-mode claim for 26.9. Clear unsupported false; the inspected primary materials do not define this capability flag.

tool_call.note: The exact 26.9 provider endpoint accepts tools and auto tool_choice; developer API documents returned assistant tool_calls. This verifies supported function-calling interface, not a reliability score.

description.value: Unbiased's proprietary composite model that combines outputs from multiple language models. This entry describes the original Pareto 26.9 release.
description.note: State the documented system design and version; avoid unsupported comparative performance or a single-checkpoint implication.

patch.notes: This record describes Pareto 26.9, publicly available as Union Alpha on September 16, 2026; the unversioned alias later moved to 26.10. Unbiased describes a proprietary blend of selected frontier/open model outputs whose composition can change. No total or active parameter count, named base checkpoint or single neural architecture is disclosed. The 262144-token context is the documented 26.9 service limit. Reasoning-mode support is unverified.

summary: Distinguishes original Pareto 26.9 from its mutable alias, corrects earliest public availability to the September 16 Union Alpha preview, adds Pareto family and proprietary license, and clears unsupported reasoning=false. Confirms 262144 hosted context, text/image input, text output and tool calls. Fresh October 27 original-source review retains undisclosed total and active counts: the changing output blend has no published model-size convention or named unchanged base lineage.

parameter_reaudit.outcome: Retain parameters_b=null and active_parameters_b=null, both undisclosed, after separate fresh review; no supported nominal size or unchanged base lineage found.

fresh_originals.finding: Mechanism section explicitly blends selected frontier/open outputs and permits composition changes, without counts or constituent names.
Names Circuit & Chisel and describes the blend; no base checkpoint lineage or size.
Identifies Union Alpha as 26.9 and separates later 26.10; no size or component lineage.
October 15 preserves 26.9 while changing alias to 26.10; no model parameter disclosure.
Later developer comparison includes 26.9 but only score and cost columns, with no total or activated size convention.
October preview compares original 26.9 and costs; no unchanged backbone or count.
Definition and section 2(c) confirm multi-model synthesis and mutable composition; no names or learned counts.
API documentation contains no learned-model count or exact constituent identity.
Stable-release note confirms several models per request and continuing 26.9 availability, without parameter accounting.
Pinned original evaluation interfaces expose optional cascade telemetry, not a named 26.9 deployment or count.

parameter_reaudit.search_findings: Bounded fresh searches for both counts, named base/post-training lineage and later original research comparisons found no additional qualifying count. The developer comparison card is the applicable later original table and supplies no active-count column. Search-only secondary leads describing undisclosed sizes were not used as primary proof; an unattributed rumoured 26.1B claim concerned 26.10-preview, not this 26.9 record, and was not adopted.
parameter_reaudit.access_limitations: The older /pareto-26-8/ URL returned HTTP 200 but only a short redirect-style page linking current scores/pricing; cached search text of that earlier version was not treated as a fresh original disclosure. All ten originals listed above were available in fresh October 27 fetches; fetch manifests are /tmp/parameter-late-model-originals/manifest.json and /tmp/parameter-512-research/manifest.json.
parameter_reaudit.remaining_uncertainty: No published nominal total, per-request active-weight convention or named unchanged base/component lineage is established. This is an evidence-bounded null, not proof that underlying models have no parameters.
